09-2.solution: The work is \(18 \times 20 = 360\) man-days. In 12 days it needs \(\frac{360}{12} = 30\) men.

09-3.solution: The wall is \(15 \times 24 = 360\) worker-days. In 8 days \(120\) are done, leaving \(240\) for 12 workers: \(20\) more days.

09-4.solution: The task is \(10 \times 8 \times 15 = 1200\) man-hours. 12 men at 10 hours a day do \(120\) a day, so \(10\) days.

09-8.solution: The trench is \(30 \times 18 = 540\) man-days. In 6 days \(180\) are done, leaving \(360\) for 36 men: \(10\) more days.

09-9.solution: One boy does \(\frac{1}{120}\) a day and one girl \(\frac{1}{120}\). Then \(4\) boys and \(6\) girls do \(\frac{10}{120} = \frac{1}{12}\) a day: \(12\) days.

09-10.solution: The project is \(20 \times 25 = 500\) worker-days. In 20 days it needs \(\frac{500}{20} = 25\) workers.

09-12.solution: The harvest is \(24 \times 16 = 384\) worker-days. 16 workers need \(\frac{384}{16} = 24\) days, which is \(8\) more than 16.

09-13.solution: The wall is \(18 \times 6 \times 20 = 2160\) man-hours. At 8 hours a day for 15 days it needs \(\frac{2160}{120} = 18\) men.

09-14.solution: One typist types \(\frac{180}{12 \times 3} = 5\) pages an hour. 300 pages in 4 hours needs \(\frac{300}{5 \times 4} = 15\) typists.

09-16.solution: Each item takes \(\frac{40 \times 10}{800} = 0.5\) worker-days. 1200 items take \(600\) worker-days, so in 12 days \(50\) workers.

09-17.solution: Each cubic metre takes \(\frac{15 \times 6}{450} = 0.2\) excavator-days. 600 cubic metres take \(120\), so in 8 days \(15\) excavators.

09-18.solution: The job is \(8 \times 7 \times 18 = 1008\) man-hours. 6 men at 8 hours a day do \(48\) a day, so \(\frac{1008}{48} = 21\) days.

09-19.solution: Each dress takes \(\frac{20 \times 5 \times 6}{80} = 7.5\) hours. 15 seamstresses for 8 days at 5 hours give \(600\) hours, so \(\frac{600}{7.5} = 80\) dresses.

09-20.solution: Each book takes \(\frac{12 \times 4 \times 10}{960} = 0.5\) printer-hours. 1440 books take \(720\); in 8 days at 6 hours that is \(\frac{720}{48} = 15\) printers.

09-21.solution: Each sapling takes \(\frac{6 \times 4 \times 5}{180} = \frac{2}{3}\) hours. 270 saplings take \(180\) hours; in 3 days at 6 hours that is \(\frac{180}{18} = 10\) gardeners.

09-22.solution: Each chair takes \(\frac{14 \times 7 \times 6}{28} = 21\) hours. 21 carpenters for 12 days at 4 hours give \(1008\) hours, so \(\frac{1008}{21} = 48\) chairs.

09-23.solution: Each loaf takes \(\frac{16 \times 8 \times 5}{320} = 2\) baker-hours. 12 bakers for 6 days at 10 hours give \(720\) hours, so \(360\) loaves.

09-24.solution: Each suit takes \(\frac{9 \times 15}{45} = 3\) tailor-days. 75 suits take \(225\), so 15 tailors need \(15\) days.

09-26.solution: Each project takes \(\frac{22 \times 14}{11} = 28\) engineer-days. 28 engineers for 18 days give \(504\), so \(18\) projects.

09-27.solution: Each product takes \(\frac{25 \times 6 \times 8}{150} = 8\) worker-hours. 30 workers for 5 days at 10 hours give \(1500\) hours, so \(\frac{1500}{8} = 187.5\) products.
